Finding Marcus Jooste

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He was a man at the top of his game but when the Steinhoff story broke, it became apparent that Markus Jooste had a lot of skeletons in his cupboard.

Unique Selling Point:
56 Year old Marcus Jooste had the world at the feet. He was the CEO of one of the biggest companies in the world. But at the end of 2017 the bubble burst and his world came crashing down.
Since then he has avoided the media, refusing interviews. Many thought that he had gone into hiding but recently he was seen dining in a Cape Town restaurant with his girlfriend Bernadine Odendaal. He has been living in his house in Hermanus.

Press Release:



Finding Markus Jooste
Markus Jooste was at the top of his game – a multi-millionaire and CEO of one of the biggest companies in the world. Then the massive Steinhoff retail empire came crashing down. As company shares plummeted, Jooste went into hiding. Carte Blanche tracks down the man at the centre of the Steinhoff turmoil.


Script:


“I think that we have done in years what other people wouldn’t dream of doing in a lifetime.”

V/O

The words of Markus Jooste the business genius, the crown prince, the man that would make the Steinhoff dream a reality.

Macfarlane Link Steinhoff has often been lauded as one of South Africa’s successful companies but on the 5th of December 2017 it all came crashing down. They wiped off almost R300b off the JSE and the man at the centre of this is Markus Jooste.

V/O

Money Web editor Ryk van Niekerk says red flags were already raised as far back as 2015 by German authorities, initiating a probe into irregularities, but the investigation fell from public view.

Ryk van Niekerk

Then on the 5th of December what happened was that Deloitte which was Steinhoff’s auditors refused to sign off financial results which means that they don’t believe the accounts of the financial statements of Steinhoff was accurate.

V/O

The company’s share price plummeted on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and CEO Markus Jooste resigned. In a personal note to employees he apologised for making big mistakes, taking sole responsibility for bringing the company to its knees.

Ryk van Niekerk Steinhoff had one of the best Boards in South Africa – highly respected board. People like Dr Steve Booysen, ex CEO of ABSA, Dr Johan van Zyl ex CEO of Sanlam, Dr Theunie Lategan a senior manager at FNB, Len Konar one of the top auditing professionals in the

country. There was six CA's on that Board, and apparently he pulled wool over their eyes.

Zwelakhe I mean it is near impossible, actually let me say it is impossible for a 6 billion euro fraud to be hidden away from auditors, the board and the CFO Ben Le Grange.

V/O Global Fund Manager Zwelakhe Mnguni has for some time doubted the integrity of the Steinhoff board.

Zwelakhe There is lack of diversity of opinion on the board, so to ask what the Steinhoff board appears to be was an old boys' club of either billionaires or multi-millionaires who are just there to rent their credibilities to provide Steinhoff with that credibility.

Ryk van Niekerk Steinhoff is not a corner shop. It is one of the biggest international furniture companies in the world. It has subsidiaries all over the world – Europe, the UK, the US, South Africa – and there are many regulatory authorities regulating what they can and cannot do. So, to pin it on one person as the only person who knew what was going on I don't think is accurate.

V/O With so many questions unanswered, a Carte Blanche team travelled to Stellenbosch in search of Markus Jooste, who, after his resignation, had gone to ground. On a tip off, we traced the Jooste family to their Hermanus holiday home... calling from the gate, we asked Mrs Ingrid Jooste for an interview

Ingrid Jooste Why do you want an interview , just stay out of our lives.

V/O Carte Blanche then sent an invitation to Mr Jooste via his attorneys requesting an interview. We received the following response:

“ …While the work on financial restatements and forensic investigations are underway, Steinhoff is legally and otherwise constrained in what it is able to communicate to the public. “

V/O The reluctance of the Jooste’s to give answers while seemingly carrying on with their luxury lifestyle has angered many in the close knit community of Hermanus. At the end of last year they started a controversial excavation on a new beach front plot.

De Waal There were huge plans for the property including underground garages and built in swimming pools and so forth...,

V/O De Waal Steyn is the editor of The Village News in Hermanus.

De Waal Theres huge holes right next to the ocean and ocean front, its empty it just doesn’t look good.

V/O Ruth Tondowski’s home is adjacent to this particular Jooste property.

Ruth

The people of the community are very upset about what has happened here. And I can't understand it, for one person for a holiday home it seems pretty horrendous to me. And now with the Steinhoff affair what is going to happen to this site.

V/O Markus Jooste was known for his lavish lifestyle and enjoyed the fruit of his success. It is claimed that he spent a total of one hundred million rand a year on his passion, racehorses. He was the man with the midas touch and it is estimated that only the ruler of the emirate of Dubai owned more horses

V/o He is described as arrogant , a tough guy, a straight talker and ladies- man.

V/o Insiders say Markus Jooste was Steinhoff.

Re-enactment The culture in the company was: Ask Markus, Markus will decide, you didn’t dare move outside of Markus’ parameters.

Corporate When Markus has a vision you cannot stop him.

Re-enactment

Markus approved everything . Everything had to be on par with standards set by Markus. Without Markus the orchestra couldn’t play.

V/O

Appearing in front of a parliamentary committee this week Acting CEO and majority shareholder, Christo Wiese, claimed that the news about so called irregularities came as a total surprise to them all

Christo Wiese

In this instance it was literally a bolt out of the blue. Now from my perspective as chairman the first time that I became aware of the impending problem literally 3 working days before the matter had to be, the accounts had to be finalised for the board meeting of December. It was absolute turmoil.

V/O At the same hearing Steinhoff Acting Chair, Heather Sonn dropped a bombshell.

Heather Sonn Based on our investigations to date we have reported former CEO, Markus Jooste to the HAWKS in terms of section 34.1B of PRECA on suspicion that he has committed offences thereunder.

Macfarlane Question Shareholders have certainly been affected but what about the ordinary

pensioner, the man on the street, how has this affected them?

Zwelakhe People underestimate what a stock market is. A stock market is a savings platform for the long term. And the people who are saving there are the cleaners on the street, are the people who are picking up garbage, people who are working in the shops. And to lose eco billion collectively for investors is a substantial amount. It is bigger than the corruption that people have been making noise about in the public sector. It's massive. There are people who are going to suffer, whose kids are not going to be able to go to school as a result of money being lost on the stock exchange. So, it is enormous and I think the industry, the investment money industry has to stand up against this kind of violation and makes sure that nothing like this happens again in our market.

Corporate UPSOUND

PROMOS:

15 sec LINK: Is Steinhoff's ex CEO Markus Jooste solely responsible for the company's collapse. With so many questions on people's lips a Carte Blanche team travelled to Stellenbosch and Hermanus in search of the man and some answers.

15 sec Markus Jooste claims to be solely responsible for the fall of Steinhoff... UPSOUND: There were 6 CA's on that board and apparently he pulled wool over their eyes.

But where’s the man at the centre of all this controversy?

10sec Early December 2017 the Steinhoff bubble burst. CEO Markus Jooste resigned, and company shares plummeted.
